section_1.title: Introduction: The Paradox of Pi
section_1.content: Introduce the counter-intuitive phenomenon: how the total number of elastic collisions between two blocks of different masses relates to the digits of π. Hook the audience by demonstrating a simulation where mass ratios lead to digit sequences.
section_1.example: Visualize two blocks, A (mass 1kg) and B (mass 100kg), colliding on a frictionless track. We count the total number of impacts until block B reverses direction.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
section_2.content: Review the Conservation of Momentum and Conservation of Kinetic Energy. Explain that for perfectly elastic collisions, these two equations uniquely define the post-collision velocities of both blocks.
section_2.example: A 'Billiard Ball' diagram showing velocity vectors changing instantly upon contact, reinforcing that the mass ratio determines the energy exchange efficiency.

section_3.title: Mapping Collisions to Phase Space
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Phase Space' concept. Instead of simple time-based tracking, we plot velocity components on a 2D plane (x-axis for Block A, y-axis for Block B). The collisions become reflections off boundary lines in this coordinate system.
section_3.example: An animation of a particle bouncing inside a triangular wedge; the angle of the wedge is determined by the mass ratio, turning collision counting into a geometry problem.

section_4.title: The Limit of Infinity (100^n)
section_4.content: Explain that as the mass ratio of the heavy block to the light block increases (e.g., 1, 100, 10,000...), the number of collisions converges to the digits of π. This links Newtonian dynamics directly to the circle constant.
section_4.example: A digital display showing: Ratio 1:1 = 3 collisions; Ratio 1:100 = 31 collisions; Ratio 1:10,000 = 314 collisions.

section_5.title: Conclusion and Intuitive Synthesis
section_5.content: Summarize how the physics system acts as an analog computer for digits of π. Emphasize that symmetry in the conservation equations mirrors the geometric symmetry of a circle, connecting movement to transcendental numbers.
section_5.example: A closing shot of a 'pi-block calculator' where a giant 1,000,000kg lead block sits on a track, awaiting a 1kg wooden cube to extract the first 6 digits of π through collision counts.
